body: {"items":[{"id":"2026-23239","title":"Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards; Modernization of FMVSS No. 108 To Accommodate ADS-Equipped Vehicles","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/16/2026-23239/federal-motor-vehicle-safety-standards-modernization-of-fmvss-no-108-to-accommodate-ads-equipped","summary":"In response to requests from the Alliance for Automotive Innovation (the Alliance), Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) International, and Gatik AI Inc. (Gatik), NHTSA is announcing a 15-day extension of the public comment period for the notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) published on October 26, 2026 proposing to amend Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 108, \"Lamps, reflective devices, and associated equipment.\" The proposed modifications would distinguish how regulations apply to vehicles with and without manually operated driving controls. The comment period for the notice was originally scheduled to end on November 25, 2026. It will now end on December 10, 2026.","publishedAt":"2026-11-16","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23238","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities; Notice and Request for Comment; 49 CFR Part 555, Temporary Exemption From Motor Vehicle Safety and Bumper Standards","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/16/2026-23238/agency-information-collection-activities-notice-and-request-for-comment-49-cfr-part-555-temporary","summary":"NHTSA invites public comments about our intention to request approval from the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for a new information collection. Before a Federal agency can collect certain information from the public, it must receive approval from OMB. Under procedures established by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, before seeking OMB approval, Federal agencies must solicit public comment on proposed collections of information, including extensions and reinstatement of previously approved collections. This document describes a collection of information for which NHTSA intends to seek OMB approval titled \"49 CFR part 555, Temporary Exemption from Motor Vehicle Safety and Bumper Standards.\"","publishedAt":"2026-11-16","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23229","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/16/2026-23229/airworthiness-directives-dassault-aviation-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Dassault Aviation Model FALCON 6X airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a determination that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-16","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23222","title":"Northern Indiana Commuter Transportation District's Request To Amend Its Positive Train Control System","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/16/2026-23222/northern-indiana-commuter-transportation-districts-request-to-amend-its-positive-train-control","summary":"This document provides the public with notice that, on November 1, 2026, the Northern Indiana Commuter Transportation District (NICD) submitted a request for amendment (RFA) to its FRA-certified positive train control (PTC) system. NICD intends to replace several Cisco Networking devices as part of a PTC hardware replacement project. This will involve three of NICD's trains, Trains 35, 432, and 601, operating without PTC technology for approximately three hours from 11:00 p.m. to 2:20 a.m. on one date that is to be determined following FRA's review and approval. FRA is publishing this notice and inviting public comment on NICD's RFA to its PTC system.","publishedAt":"2026-11-16","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23213","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/16/2026-23213/airworthiness-directives-airbus-helicopters-deutschland-gmbh-ahd-helicopters","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model MBB-BK 117 C-1 and MBB-BK 117 C-2 helicopters with a certain air conditioning system installed in accordance with FAA Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) No. SR00601DE. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of corrosion on the condenser inlet duct, which caused the internal support wire helix to impinge the tail rotor (TR) drive shaft. This proposed AD would require repetitively inspecting the TR drive shaft; repetitively inspecting the exterior of the Air Comm Corporation (ACC) condenser duct assembly (duct assembly); repetitively inspecting (using a borescope) the interior of the ACC duct assembly; and depending on the results of these inspections, replacing certain parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-16","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23212","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/16/2026-23212/airworthiness-directives-airbus-helicopters","summary":"The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-24-01, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Model EC 155 B and EC 155 B1 helicopters. AD 2025-24-01 requires replacement of the jettisonable windows and seals on the sliding doors and fixed panels on the left-hand (LH) and right-hand (RH) sides and the installation of new labels. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-24-01, the manufacturer determined the applicable service information was missing procedures for the tinted windows. This proposed AD would require the same actions as AD 2025-24-01 and would additionally require new actions to include helicopters with the modification of tinted windows. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-16","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23209","title":"Pipeline Safety: Meetings of the Liquid and Gas Pipeline Advisory Committees","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/16/2026-23209/pipeline-safety-meetings-of-the-liquid-and-gas-pipeline-advisory-committees","summary":"This notice announces public meetings of the Technical Pipeline Safety Standards Committee, also known as the Gas Pipeline Advisory Committee (GPAC), and the Technical Hazardous Liquid Pipeline Safety Standards Committee, also known as the Liquid Pipeline Advisory Committee (LPAC). The meetings will be held to discuss the notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM), titled \"Repair Criteria for Hazardous Liquid and Gas Transmission Pipelines.\"","publishedAt":"2026-11-16","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23207","title":"Qualification of Drivers; Exemption Applications; Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillators (ICD)","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/16/2026-23207/qualification-of-drivers-exemption-applications-implantable-cardioverter-defibrillators-icd","summary":"FMCSA announces receipt of applications from five individuals for an exemption from the prohibition in the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (FMCSRs) against operation of a commercial motor vehicle (CMV) by persons with a current clinical diagnosis of myocardial infarction, angina pectoris, coronary insufficiency, thrombosis, or any other cardiovascular disease of a variety known to be accompanied by syncope (transient loss of consciousness), dyspnea (shortness of breath), collapse, or congestive heart failure. If granted, the exemption would enable the individual with an ICD to operate CMVs in interstate commerce.","publishedAt":"2026-11-16","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23201","title":"Petition for Exemption; Summary of Petition Received; Blue Vigil, LLC","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/16/2026-23201/petition-for-exemption-summary-of-petition-received-blue-vigil-llc","summary":"This notice contains a summary of a petition seeking relief from specified requirements of Federal Aviation Regulations. The purpose of this notice is to improve the public's awareness of, and participation in, the FAA's exemption process. Neither publication of this notice nor the inclusion nor omission of information in the summary is intended to affect the legal status of the petition or its final disposition.","publishedAt":"2026-11-16","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23198","title":"Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23198/airworthiness-directives-the-boeing-company-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 787-8 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report that certain wing skin outer mold line (OML) penetrating fasteners installed using threaded nuts without cap seals do not provide reliable protection against potential ignition sources when subjected to direct attachment lightning currents. This proposed AD would require inspecting between certain ribs on the left and right wing for wing skin penetrating fasteners with a threaded nut adjacent to the electromagnetic effects (EME) sleeve; inspecting the left and right wing fuel tanks, surge tanks, and dry bays for threaded nuts installed on fasteners that penetrate the upper and lower wing skins; accomplishing the inspection specified in a certain airworthiness limitation (AWL); and applicable on-condition actions. This proposed AD would also require accomplishing concurrent requirements and revising the maintenance program to incorporate the airworthiness limitation task. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-13","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23194","title":"Amendment of Class C Airspace; Laughlin Air Force Base, Del Rio, TX","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23194/amendment-of-class-c-airspace-laughlin-air-force-base-del-rio-tx","summary":"This action makes administrative amendments to the Laughlin AFB, TX, Class C airspace legal description. Specifically, the action updates the geographic coordinates of the airport reference point (ARP) to match the FAA's National Airspace System Resources (NASR) database information. Additionally, this action corrects the header format to conform with current FAA policy. Lastly, this action updates the outdated term \"Airport/Facility Directory\" to \"Chart Supplement.\" This action does not change the lateral boundaries, altitudes, or operating requirements of the Class C airspace area.","publishedAt":"2026-11-13","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23134","title":"Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23134/airworthiness-directives-the-boeing-company-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all The Boeing Company Model 747-400 and 747-400F series airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of an overheated alternating current motor pump (ACMP) that caused a fire in the main landing gear (MLG) wheel well. This proposed AD would require a maintenance records check or inspection for any installed ACMP with a certain part number and applicable on-condition actions. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-13","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23118","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Pratt & Whitney Canada Corp. Engines","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23118/airworthiness-directives-pratt-and-whitney-canada-corp-engines","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Pratt & Whitney Canada Corp. (P&WC) Model PW814GA and PW815GA engines. This proposed AD was prompted by the manufacturer revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing airworthiness limitations manual (ALM) to introduce new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. This proposed AD would require updating the ALS of the existing ALM or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive instructions and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-13","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23116","title":"Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23116/airworthiness-directives-general-electric-company-engines","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain General Electric Company (GE) Model GE Passport 20-17BB1A, GE Passport 20-18BB1A, GE Passport 20-19BB1A, and GE Passport 20-19BB1B engines. This proposed AD was prompted by an engine in-flight shutdown (IFSD) due to an engine fire caused by fuel leakage within the engine core compartment. This proposed AD would require replacement of a certain start bleed valve (SBV) fuel tube with a redesigned SBV fuel tube. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-13","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23111","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities: Requests for Comments; Clearance of Renewed Approval of Information Collection: Noise Certification Standards for Subsonic Jet Airplanes and Subsonic Transport Category Large Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23111/agency-information-collection-activities-requests-for-comments-clearance-of-renewed-approval-of","summary":"In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FAA invites public comments about our intention to request the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) approval to renew an information collection. The collection involves the noise certification regulations of 14 CFR part 36 for aircraft. This includes information collection requirements for the noise certification of subsonic aircraft-jet airplanes and subsonic transport category large airplanes, small propeller driven airplanes and rotorcraft. The information collected are the results of noise certification tests that demonstrate compliance with 14 CFR part 36. The original information collection was implemented to show compliance in accordance with the Aircraft Noise Abatement Act of 1968; that statute is now part of the overall codification of the FAA's regulatory authority over aircraft noise in 49 U.S.C. 44715. The noise compliance report is used by the FAA in making a finding that the airplane is in noise compliance with the regulations. These compliance reports are required only once when an applicant wants to certificate an aircraft type. Without this data collection, the FAA would be unable to make the required noise certification compliance finding.","publishedAt":"2026-11-13","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23109","title":"Amendment of Class C Airspace; President Donald J. Trump International Airport, FL","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/13/2026-23109/amendment-of-class-c-airspace-president-donald-j-trump-international-airport-fl","summary":"This action proposes to amend Class C airspace at the President Donald J. Trump International Airport (DJT), West Palm Beach, FL. The FAA is proposing this action to enhance the efficient management of air traffic operations and reduce the potential for midair collision in the West Palm Beach, FL, terminal area.","publishedAt":"2026-11-13","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23074","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/12/2026-23074/airworthiness-directives-dassault-aviation-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Dassault Aviation Model MYSTERE-FALCON 50, FALCON 2000, and FALCON 2000EX airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a reported quality escape and a determination that high-temperature oxidation of main landing gear (MLG) upper and lower torque links may have occurred during manufacturing. This proposed AD would require replacing any affected MLG with a serviceable MLG. This proposed AD would also limit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-12","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23073","title":"Standard Instrument Approach Procedures, and Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures; Miscellaneous Amendments","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/12/2026-23073/standard-instrument-approach-procedures-and-takeoff-minimums-and-obstacle-departure-procedures","summary":"This rule amends, suspends, or removes Standard Instrument Approach Procedures (SIAPs) and associated Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures for operations at certain airports. These regulatory actions are needed because of the adoption of new or revised criteria, or because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System, such as the commissioning of new navigational facilities, adding new obstacles, or changing air traffic requirements. These changes are designed to provide for the safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace and to promote safe flight operations under instrument flight rules at the affected airports.","publishedAt":"2026-11-12","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23072","title":"Standard Instrument Approach Procedures, and Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures; Miscellaneous Amendments","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/12/2026-23072/standard-instrument-approach-procedures-and-takeoff-minimums-and-obstacle-departure-procedures","summary":"This rule establishes, amends, suspends, or removes Standard Instrument Approach Procedures (SIAPS) and associated Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure procedures (ODPs) for operations at certain airports. These regulatory actions are needed because of the adoption of new or revised criteria, or because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System, such as the commissioning of new navigational facilities, adding new obstacles, or changing air traffic requirements. These changes are designed to provide safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace and to promote safe flight operations under instrument flight rules at the affected airports.","publishedAt":"2026-11-12","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23068","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Diamond Aircraft Industries GmbH Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/12/2026-23068/airworthiness-directives-diamond-aircraft-industries-gmbh-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Diamond Aircraft Industries GmbH (DAI) Model DA 50 C airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of flap actuator failures. This proposed AD would require inspecting for displacement of the black slide grommet and inspecting the rod end bearing for a tight fit of the flap actuator. This proposed AD would also require modification of the flap actuator followed by repetitive inspections for a broken actuator torque seal on the jam nuts at the attachment of the rod end bearing of the flap actuator with applicable corrective action. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of unmodified flap actuators on any airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-12","source":"Federal Register"}]}
